Crypto just had its biggest drop in stablecoin supply since June 2022.

That's $14.2B less in circulation in just 30 days.

So where did all that liquidity go?

I looked into the data, and there's pretty strong evidence of investors cashing out:

→ USDT/USDC supply fell by ~$11B
→ Stablecoin off-ramping doubled in a week (mostly USDT sold for USD)
→ Spot BTC ETFs had $1.6B in net outflows over 20 trading sessions

The recent Binance hack probably didn't help investor confidence either.

Seeing this much liquidity leave circulation while BTC struggles to recover is a bad look rn.

Not a great end of year compared to some previous ones.

#uranium #copper #silver #gold

⚡ THE DAILY METALS PULSE | 13 NOVEMBER 2026

Gold is attempting a recovery after Thursday’s 3% plunge. But the US 10-year yield reached 5.14% overnight, while Brent is back around $95–96 as Middle East supply risks return.

Today, producer inflation tests whether the Fed needs to move faster.

☢️ URANIUM

Oklo and Centrus have signed definitive, multi-year agreements for advanced-reactor fuel, with deliveries scheduled from 2029.

The important detail: prepayments will help finance new US enrichment capacity. Future electricity demand is becoming funded fuel procurement, not just reactor announcements.

🟠 COPPER

Copper is near $6.16/lb after LME metal closed 1.37% lower at $13,605 per tonne.

There is a fresh development beneath the macro selloff: delayed imports are reaching China. SMM reports inventories rose roughly 5,000 tonnes from Monday, while Shanghai spot premiums fell.

Stocks remain historically low, but the immediate squeeze is easing. Uncertainty around AI infrastructure investment adds another headwind.

🥈 SILVER

Silver is hovering around $50/oz, below yesterday morning’s $51.40.

Higher yields pressure its monetary appeal. Copper’s weakness adds an industrial headwind.

A softer inflation report could help both sides. Another upside surprise would leave silver particularly exposed.

🥇 GOLD

Gold is trading around $3,900/oz after Thursday’s fall to its lowest since October 2025.

Overnight, New York Fed President John Williams said further hikes are likely. That gives buyers little policy relief despite the modest rebound.

Gold needs more than bargain hunting. It needs yields and the dollar to stop climbing.

📍 TODAY’S WATCH

US PPI: 14:30 CET / 08:30 ET.

Consensus: +0.4% headline and +0.3% core month over month.

Watch the underlying components, not just energy. A broad upside surprise could strengthen the case for faster tightening; softer figures could give battered metals breathing room.

Oil is rebuilding inflation risk.
Bonds are pricing tighter money.
PPI is today’s next test.

Follow @Swedish_Uranium for the next pulse.

To me privacy pools type tech is a good keyhole solution: it serves the goal of making thieves' lives significantly harder (though it may require harsher measures: 24h deposit delay, and charge some small fee on rejection) without doing the really harmful thing: backdoors.

No backdoors is the line that is defensible as an absolute.

Long-term though, we really need to upgrade everyone to much safer storage formats for coins.
